issues.title: Bundled root certificates trust compromised eMudhra (emSign) intermediate CAs
issues.summary: Bun's default trust store included the root 'emSign ECC Root CA - G3'. Eight eMudhra (emSign) intermediate CAs were revoked for key compromise (disclosed 2026-10-17/20); six issue TLS certificates chaining to that root. Bun <=1.4.3 accepts certificates from those intermediates by default, and only checks revocation against a CRL passed explicitly via the `crl` option, so the CA's own revocation has no effect by default.
issues.applicability: Affects any default-trust-store TLS connection: fetch(), bun install/bunx, node:https, node:tls, WebSocket, Bun.connect. --use-system-ca / NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1 does not help (adds to the bundled roots, does not replace them). Executables built with `bun build --compile` embed the affected trust store and stay vulnerable until rebuilt with a fixed Bun.
issues.fixed_in: 1.4.4 (removes the emSign G3/C1/C3 roots from the bundle, updates to NSS 3.131.1, and rejects chains containing the 8 compromised keys with CERT_REVOKED)
issues.workaround: Pass an explicit CA list that excludes the emSign roots: the `ca` option per connection, `--cafile` for bun install, or `cafile` in bunfig.toml.

related_incident.note: No SHA-256 fingerprints or serial numbers for the 8 compromised intermediates were published in any source checked as of last_updated.

issues.title: Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write, can lead to RCE
issues.summary: The same Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write fixed in Node.js 22.23.4/24.22.1/26.12.1 (CVE-2026-111497) affects Bun's own Brotli implementation.
issues.applicability: Applies to any code path that Brotli-decompresses attacker-influenced data: explicit Bun/zlib Brotli APIs, or implicitly via HTTP honoring Content-Encoding: br / Accept-Encoding: br.
issues.workaround: None documented other than upgrading; avoid accepting attacker-controlled Brotli-encoded input on affected versions if upgrading is not immediately possible.
